key_insight: CNNs, ViTs, and Vision Mamba show different attention patterns, and their saliency alignment with human gaze varies by task and architecture.
clinical_relevance: Understanding which model attention better matches human visual focus can improve trust and interpretability in medical imaging AI, especially for high-stakes decisions.
method: Compared CNN, ViT, and Vision Mamba architectures across fine-grained classification, medical imaging, and emotion recognition.
Mapped post-hoc attribution maps and eye-tracking heatmaps into standardized spatial probability distributions.
Evaluated alignment using Jensen-Shannon similarity, Chi-square similarity, and Pearson correlation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports gaze-based validation across multiple datasets/tasks, revealing strong task-dependent alignment differences and cases where support overlap is high but linear correlation is low.
watch_item: Attention alignment metrics can disagree with each other, so high overlap does not necessarily mean the model matches human visual behavior in a meaningful way.
paper_title: Bridging Human and Model Attention: Explainability Analysis of CNN, Mamba, and ViT Architectures with Gaze-Based Validation
